nearest_visible_records.stem: A patient requested a partial fill of Dexedrine at this pharmacy 12 days after issue and returns for the documented balance on day 28. Which rule controls?

choices.text: Use the 72-hour rule for a pharmacy stock shortage.
Calculate 30 days from the date of the partial dispensing.
Send the balance to any pharmacy selected by the patient.
Dispense the documented remainder at the same pharmacy before the 30-day issue-date deadline.
Record the balance as an authorized refill of the Schedule II prescription.

nearest_visible_records.stem:
Case A: An emergency oral Schedule II prescription is partially filled at the patient's request, and staff apply the ordinary nonemergency 30-day requested-partial window.

Case B: A Massachusetts patient asks a different pharmacy in the same chain to provide a remainder after an initial requested partial fill at the first pharmacy.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Shortage and emergency requested partial use one identical starting event merely because both say 72 hours.
The same chain name makes every location the same pharmacy for the requested remainder.
Any remaining quantity counts as an initially unfilled EPCS eligible for initial transfer.
The federal emergency-oral requested-partial remainder limit is 72 hours from issuance rather than the ordinary 30-day period.

nearest_visible_records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy partially fills a Schedule II prescription at the patient's request two days after the prescription was issued. On day 29 after issuance, the patient asks a different pharmacy to dispense the balance because the first pharmacy is closed. On day 31, the patient returns to the first pharmacy for the balance. Which assessment is correct?

choices.text: The second pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 29 because the federal 30-day period has not expired.
The first pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 31 because the 30 days run from the initial partial fill.
Either pharmacy may dispense the balance if it can access the original prescription electronically.
Neither requested dispensing is permitted: only the pharmacy that made the partial fill may dispense the balance, and it must do so no later than 30 days after issuance.
Neither requested dispensing is permitted because every Schedule II remainder is due within 72 hours of the partial fill.

choices.text: A lawful initial partial starts a fresh 30-day remainder period.

The second remainder is evaluated using the separate issuance-based remainder clock and other conditions.

The ordinary Schedule VI drug is not brought within the rule merely by its Schedule VI classification.
A familiar customer may receive a covered drug without identification or the documented hardship procedure.

Case A: A prescriber is about to prescribe an applicable Schedule II opioid and proposes skipping the required PMP check because the pharmacy will submit dispensing data later.

Case B: Staff conclude that gabapentin's inclusion in dispensing reports automatically places it in every specifically enumerated opioid or benzodiazepine query category.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Every Schedule IV drug is a benzodiazepine for the query rule.
Holding a pharmacist license exempts the person from duties arising when legally prescribing.
